A quick reminder of the one trap at this level: the verb "be" can disappear in fast writing, especially after a long subject. "The students in my class tired today" is missing "are"; the subject is plural, so it needs "are" even though "class" sits right before the gap.

Your task: write two sentences of your own about people you know. In the first, use a long subject (for example, a person plus a detail about them). In the second, use "we" or "they" and describe how the people feel. Check that each sentence has the right form of "be" and that it agrees with the real subject, not the nearest noun.
